teams.heading: Sewabu says only around 10 Japan players joined White's Lyon camp
teams.body: Fiji Rugby chief executive Kali Sewabu has said only about 10 players from the Japan match have travelled to Europe, with the rest drawn from the European-based pool. White and that group flew from Tokyo straight into a three-day camp in Lyon, and Sewabu called limited preparation time the 'normal challenge and barrier for Fiji rugby'. He said White wanted to see the whole squad before naming the final squad, a call that has since been made.

lead.why: It is the one Fiji-specific item not already reported, and it explains how White's preparation is being squeezed.

teams.heading: England's Alex Mitchell limps off with suspected hamstring pull before Wallabies
teams.body: Alex Mitchell limped off Northampton's 28-14 win over Gloucester with a suspected hamstring pull, and the Guardian describes him as a major doubt for England's autumn opener against Australia. It is a fourth hamstring injury this year, and Archie McParland, his Saints team-mate and fellow scrum-half, missed the game with a calf injury sustained at England's training camp. Fin Smith, Northampton's fly-half, is already sidelined with a calf injury.

lead.why: A fresh injury to England's first-choice scrum-half, days before the Australia test, is the item fans will be talking about.

teams.heading: Dan Sheehan's no8 run worked for Leinster, but Foley doubts a repeat
teams.body: Leinster's experiment with Ireland hooker Dan Sheehan at no8 against Munster worked, and Sheehan made the most carries of any player, 17. Irish Mirror columnist Derek Foley doubts Leinster will repeat it. Foley points to the no8's control of five-metre scrums, a job Leinster gave to Jamison Gibson-Park, and to Sheehan's limits as a lineout jumper and defensive option. With Caelan Doris, Jack Conan and Josh Ericson injured, Leinster were short of back-row options, Foley notes.

lead.why: The only shortlist item that is men's 15s and about an Ireland hooker, since the other men's items are the already-reported Benson story and the women's WXV coverage.

teams.heading: Valorugby Emilia beat Fiamme Oro 38-31 in Coppa Italia Girone 2
teams.body: Italian club rugby, not the Azzurri, but Valorugby Emilia moved to the top of Coppa Italia Girone 2 with a 38-31 win at Fiamme Oro in Rome on Saturday. Casilio opened the scoring and Hugo kicked six from six, as the visitors led 28-17 at half-time and held on in the second half. The result leaves Valorugby on 20 points, ahead of Fiamme Oro on 17 and Viadana on 15.

lead.why: It is the strongest new item in the pack, and it is a result that changes the Girone 2 table.

teams.heading: Finn Russell talks Henry Pollock, Eddie Hearn and Scotland's All Blacks bid
teams.body: Finn Russell has spoken to the Daily Mail about sharing the spotlight with Henry Pollock, life under Eddie Hearn and Scotland's bid to make history against the All Blacks. The backdrop is a long record: New Zealand have won 31 meetings, two have been drawn and Scotland have won none, according to BBC Scotland's Tom English. Scotland meet the All Blacks at Murrayfield on Saturday, having beaten Fiji 33-17 last time out.

lead.why: It is the only NEW item in the shortlist, and it is a Scotland player talking about the All Blacks test.

teams.heading: Wales wing Josh Adams scores as Cardiff shut out Ospreys 26-0
teams.body: Wales wing Josh Adams was released from the national squad to play for Cardiff in Saturday's Welsh derby, and he scored in a 26-0 win at St Helen's. Released to get much-needed minutes, the 31-year-old had played just twice this season. Cardiff's red-zone defence did the damage, keeping the Ospreys off the scoresheet for the first time in over two years. Adams's score came from a grubber by centre Steff Emanuel, who was involved in all three first-half tries.

lead.why: The only NEW item with a direct Wales angle, as Wales released wing Josh Adams to play for Cardiff.

teams.heading: Santiago Carreras and Thomas Gallo ruled out of Argentina squad through injury
teams.body: Argentina lost two first-choice players on the eve of their London camp, with Santiago Carreras (Bath) and Thomas Gallo (Lyon) ruled out by injury. Mateo Soler (Dogos) and Rodrigo Martínez (Dragons) came in, and Contepomi's side is also waiting on Santiago Chocobares (Toulouse), whose HIA outcome is pending, with Matías Moroni (Bristol Bears) on stand-by. Gallo and Carreras are both out with longterm injuries.

lead.why: It is a genuinely new injury story about Argentina's own squad, distinct from the Isa recall and roster coverage already read.

teams.heading: Harry McLaughlin-Phillips shines as Australia A beat USA 52-0 in New Jersey
teams.body: Australia A completed a clean sweep of the USA with a 52-0 win over the Eagles in New Jersey, and the standout was Harry McLaughlin-Phillips, who scored a try, piled on 17 points and set up at least three others. Several Wallabies hopefuls stood up, with Mac Grealy, name-dropped by coach Les Kiss over the weekend, among the backs with five-pointers and three line breaks. Zac Lomax, playing his first international match, improved as the game went on. The Eagles never scored, trailing 33-0 at the break.

lead.why: The most talked-about Wallabies item in today's pack, with several named hopefuls making a case for selection.

teams.heading: Patrick Tuipulotu and Sam Darry omitted from All Blacks' northern squad
teams.body: Patrick Tuipulotu and Sam Darry are both missing from the 36-man squad for New Zealand's northern leg of the Nations Championship, with Crusaders lock Jamie Hannah getting the nod ahead of them. Stephen Donald called Tuipulotu "hugely unlucky" on The Aftermatch with Kirst and Beav, and picked out Darry, who started two Tests in Rugby's Greatest Rivalry, as another unlucky omission. Dave Rennie's engine room options now include Scott Barrett, Josh Lord, Fabian Holland and Tupou Vaa'i.

lead.why: A new squad-selection story about New Zealand's own omissions, not the Fainga'anuku item already run today or Kirwan's piece from yesterday.

teams.heading: Steve Hansen says Erasmus is resting Etzebeth ahead of World Cup
teams.body: Steve Hansen believes Erasmus is using the November Nations Championship to rest key Springboks, with Eben Etzebeth the clearest example. Cheslin Kolbe, Etzebeth, Andre Esterhuizen and Handré Pollard are all out of the touring squad through injury, and six uncapped players have been included to cover. Speaking on the Rugby Unity podcast, Hansen said: "There's no doubt about that with Etzebeth." He thinks Erasmus is gambling with younger selections but expects his strongest group to start when it matters.

lead.why: It is a new national-team squad story naming injured Springboks and the uncapped call-ups, and it is not a repeat of the Furlong or Bulls items already reported.
